name: Tàihé A Bāo 泰和A包
description: Tàihé A Bāo (泰和A包) is a Chinese climbing game from Taihe county, Jiangxi province. Four players: one declarer vs the other three each hand. 40-card deck (remove 2s, 3s, 8s); rank A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 7, 6, 5, 4. Cards drawn from deck counterclockwise (not dealt). Bidding: declare or pass; if all pass, second round—call for a card (exchange); last caller is declarer. Play: declarer leads combinations; others beat or pass. Combinations: singles, pairs, sequences, double sequences, three-of-a-kind, four-of-a-kind (bombs beat any non-bomb). First out wins; if declarer wins they collect stakes from each opponent. Often played for money.

Chinese climbing game from Taihe (泰和) county, Jiangxi (江西) province. A correspondent learned it there around 2013. Name refers to the Ace (A) as highest card. Part of the broader Chinese climbing/shedding family.
The deck is shuffled and placed face-down in the center. Each player receives 10 cards by taking one card at a time in turn in counterclockwise order.

items.text: Five players: Five players; each receives eight cards. A hand declared in the first round of bidding is worth six stakes against each opponent.
Three players: Remove the Ace of Spades; 39 cards. Each player receives 13 cards. A set of three Aces counts as four Aces (unbeatable). First-round declare worth four stakes per opponent.

Without Aces: Kings are highest. Kings may be exchanged in bidding and used in sequences. Five players: also remove King of Spades, seven cards each. Three players: 12 cards each, deck otherwise unchanged.
